comment: CARRIERS THE TABLE DID NOT KNOW. Every row here was invisible to the differential, because `deriveHtmlEdges` and the analyzer shared one carrier list: independently written derivation over a SHARED PREMISE. A differential cannot catch a shared premise, and `otp`/`sqlite` contain none of these constructs, so 100% coverage never had to confront them. A census of 4,035 real files for URL-bearing (tag, attr) pairs found them; see script/m14/verify-carrier-census.ts.

expectRelationships.comment: The refresh PRAGMA is a NAVIGATION the browser performs — the same class as a form action, so `uses` and never `calls`. 40 occurrences across 26 files of one corpus, and absent from both tables until the census looked for it.
`http-equiv` is matched case-insensitively and `url=` needs no space after the `;` — both are how it is written in practice.

The destination is frequently a character reference, and the content is DECODED before it is parsed. A decode is not length-preserving, so parsing the raw text and indexing it with decoded offsets once published `quot;/entity-quoted&quot` as a path.
A later refresh after a bare interval is still a refresh; the `;` split takes the FIRST statement's shape and the url is read from the remainder.
Exactly ONE decode: `&` becomes `&` once. A second pass would collapse `&amp;` two levels, so the decode is owned by one caller and the other is told it already happened.
SVG2 spells a script's source `href`, not `src`. Keyed on the tag and not the namespace, which is safe because an HTML `<script>` has no `href` to read.
`feImage` pulls an image into the filter RESULT — a fetch like any other. The tag is lowercased by the walker, so the key is `feimage`.
The legacy `xlink:href` spelling reaches the same rule; the attribute map is already lowercased.

`ping` is whitespace-separated with no descriptor, so it takes a list, not a `srcset` candidate split — one row per URL, and it is a FETCH rather than a navigation because the browser requests it and the user never goes there.

A citation is a written reference out of the document, so it is an edge — graded `usage_contextual` rather than inheriting `import_based`, because the tier classifier reads that field and a citation is not a structural fetch.
Deprecated in HTML5 and still fetched by every shipping browser, so the dependency is real; the `legacy-` resourceType says so at the edge.

THE MEASURED GAP (carrier census, 2026-10-28): the legacy `background` attribute's owners are body, table, td and th, and this lane emitted only the first two. A corpus document carries a real `td@background` image that no table claimed, so the edge the browser fetches was absent from the graph.

THE SIBLING CELL, added in the same commit. `th` differs from `td` in nothing the legacy `background` attribute is concerned with, so pinning one and not the other would pin the corpus rather than the construct.

forbidRelationships.comment: `charset` is not `refresh`, so `content` is free text and never a URL. The `http-equiv` gate is what stops a description or a charset string from becoming an edge to a sentence.
`content="5"` is a bare interval: it reloads THIS document, which names nothing new. Emitting an edge here would point the document at itself.
